context: Isolated synthetic business episode; dates/amounts/contracts/people below are case-specific source facts, not new enduring Frostline policy.

records.statement: Tuesday 10:20, cold spell. Northbank Property Holdings Ltd is the active customer; Priya Shah is facilities manager at Northbank House, Manchester. Only floors 4–5 are cold; floors 0–3 remain comfortable. Portable electric heaters are being used. No smoke, water leak, unusual smell or alarm is reported.

The account summary says reactive labour for covered assets is included in normal hours. Parts and specialist subcontractors are chargeable unless specifically included. Visible contract lists boilers, pumps and AHUs; refurbished upper-floor controls coverage is unclear. Annual maintenance PO exists without demonstrated reactive scope.

Two boilers serve heating zones. Floors 4–5 were refurbished by another contractor eighteen months ago. Generic upper-floor controls entry has no confirmed model or panel location. Three weeks ago an engineer reset an intermittently communicating controller and recommended a controls survey; no survey quotation was accepted.

Samir can arrive approximately 12:00 and is competent on boilers, pumps and conventional controls, but not advanced BMS. Ellie, controls specialist, is commissioning a project until about 14:30 and could arrive about 15:15 if released on time. Moving her requires Service Manager Helen Brooks and project-manager agreement. Helen is available for urgent contact and leaves a meeting at 10:45.

Priya can arrange plant-room and floor access and normal induction. Managing-agent key for refurbished controls riser is not confirmed. No engineer has accepted dispatch. Coordinator can dispatch routine work where coverage and competence are clear; no exceptional cost/resource authority is established.

request: Priya asks for urgent attendance under the contract and heating restored before the managing director arrives at 15:00. Take control of the call and arrange the next operational step.
